headline: Demand stays strong as tariffs and currency squeeze margins
summary_short: Birkenstock's fiscal second-quarter revenue rose 7.7% y/y to €618.3 million on broad-based demand, but net profit fell 22.1% y/y to €81.9 million as U.S. tariffs, currency translation and an acquisition-related cost mark-up compressed margins.
summary_long: Revenue grew 8% y/y (14% cc) to €618.3 million, led by 22% APAC growth, though FX cut over 600bp from reported growth and the Middle East conflict cost EMEA about €6 million. Gross margin fell 380bp to 53.9% on FX (-230bp), U.S. tariffs (-90bp), the Birkenstock Australia distributor mark-up (-70bp) and channel mix. Net profit fell 22% y/y to €81.9 million on margin compression plus higher finance costs, including a €15 million non-cash embedded-derivative revaluation loss. Cash fell to €201.5 million from €329.1 million at fiscal year-end (seasonal), lifting net leverage to 1.7x from 1.5x. No formal FY2026 revenue or EPS guidance was issued; tariffs and FX are each expected to weigh on FY2026 margins by ~100bp.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by higher footwear pairs sold across all channels and segments, led by APAC (+22%); FX cut over 600bp from reported growth and the Middle East conflict cost EMEA about €6 million.

Gross profit dollars rose only slightly as margin fell 380bp to 53.9%, driven by FX (-230bp), incremental U.S. tariffs (-90bp), the Birkenstock Australia distributor mark-up (-70bp) and channel mix (-30bp).

Profit from operations fell as the same tariff, FX and distributor mark-up pressures hit cost of sales, while a €7.0 million FX loss (versus a €2.6 million gain a year ago) further weighed on the line.

Net profit fell as margin compression flowed through and finance costs rose to €33.8 million from €25.6 million, including a €15 million non-cash embedded-derivative revaluation loss on the senior notes.
Reported EBITDA fell 7.6% y/y; management's own Adjusted EBITDA (which excludes acquisition and FX items) was down just 1% at a 32.1% margin, down 270bp on FX and tariffs, partly offset by pricing.
No formal FY2026 revenue or EPS guidance was given; management reiterated that incremental U.S. tariffs and FX are each expected to weigh on FY2026 margins by roughly 100 basis points.
